userPrompt:
Suspense breaks Claude Code's prompt cache on nearly every prompt, and it's
using up my usage. In the session logs, each new prompt in a conversation
reads only Claude Code's own ~10k-token system prompt from cache and writes
the whole rest of the conversation to cache again, up to 900k+ tokens a
prompt. That's roughly 60% of this project's usage over the last three days.

The cause: we pass our instructions with --append-system-prompt and
--system-prompt-snapshot off, and they differ from one prompt to the next:
- ${UNDERSTANDING_FILE} is a new path for every task,
- each mode (Code, Spec, Combined, Ask) has its own template,
- a handoff (Code→Spec, a chain's code step) adds the other task's prompt and
  result,
- asks fork the conversation with their own system prompt.
The system prompt comes before the conversation, so any change to it
invalidates the cache for everything after it.

The fix: a conversation's system prompt must be identical, byte for byte, on
every prompt sent in it, whatever the mode. Anything that changes from prompt
to prompt goes in that prompt's message instead.
- The system prompt holds only what's the same for the whole project: the
  spec-reading prompt, the Piton fluency, and the code and spec locations.
  Build it the same way every time, with no paths, timestamps, or anything
  specific to a task, so it only changes when the project's templates or
  fluency change.
- Each prompt's message starts with a clearly marked block holding its mode's
  instructions (with ${UNDERSTANDING_FILE} filled in), and any handoff
  content, followed by the prompt itself.
- The fluency is sent once per conversation, in the system prompt, and never
  repeated in a prompt's message. The same goes for ${SPEC_READING}.
- Asks, which fork the task's conversation, send the same system prompt as
  the conversation they fork, so the fork reuses its cache.
- Freeform stays free of our instructions: no instructions block in its
  message. A Freeform prompt sent in an existing conversation keeps that
  conversation's system prompt, so the cache holds. A new conversation
  started in Freeform has none.
- For harnesses that take no system prompt of their own (Codex, OpenCode),
  the system prompt goes ahead of the first prompt of a conversation only,
  not ahead of every prompt.
- The templates saved in .suspense/system-prompts split accordingly: a
  project-wide one for the system prompt, and the mode and handoff templates
  for the per-prompt block. Saved templates that still use ${PITON_FLUENCY} or
  ${SPEC_READING} in a mode template must not end up sending the fluency with
  every prompt. Decide how to migrate them and say what you chose.
- The raw prompt modal shows what's actually sent: the system prompt, and the
  message with its instructions block.

Spec first: update the spec wherever it describes the system prompts, their
templates, the raw prompt modal, and what the harness is sent. Then change the
code to match.

Tests: using the fake harness the tests already use, check that every prompt
sent in one conversation, across Code, Spec, Combined, Ask, Freeform, and a
chain's handoff, passes the exact same --append-system-prompt, and that the
understanding path and the mode's instructions end up in the message. Then
confirm it against the real thing: send two prompts in one conversation in
different modes with the real claude, and check that the second one's
stream-json usage shows cache_read_input_tokens covering the first prompt's
context, not just ~10k.

content.text:
Every prompt in a conversation now sends the same system prompt, byte for byte, whatever its mode, and I confirmed the cache holds with the real `claude`. The code is done and tested. The spec isn't changed yet: this prompt came in Code mode, which forbids editing `./spec`, and the app's mode guard reverts spec edits from a Code task. The spec wording is at the end, ready to send in Spec or Chain mode.

**Check against the real `claude`** (Haiku, to spend less of your usage; caching works the same way). I sent two prompts in one conversation, first Code, then Spec resuming it, with the app's exact flags and this project's real system prompt:

| Prompt | Read from cache | Written to cache |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (Code) | 13,694 (Claude Code's own) | 32,911 |
| 2 (Spec, resumed) | **46,605** | 294 |

46,605 is exactly the first prompt's read plus its write, so the second prompt reused the entire conversation. Before this change it would have read only about 13.7k and written everything else again.

**What's sent now**
- **System prompt:** the project's own, from a new template, `.suspense/system-prompts/system.md`. It holds the code and spec locations, the spec-reading prompt and the fluency. It has no paths or task details, and isn't compiled per prompt, so it only changes when the templates or fluency change.
- **Message:** each prompt starts with a `<task-instructions>` block holding the mode's instructions, with the understanding path filled in and any handoff text, then the prompt itself. The fluency and spec reading are never repeated there.
- **Questions:** sent the same project system prompt, so a forked conversation reuses the cache.
- **Freeform:** no instructions block. Carrying on a conversation, it sends that conversation's own system prompt, which each conversation now remembers. Starting a new one, it sends none.
- **Codex and OpenCode:** the system prompt goes ahead of a conversation's first prompt only.
- **Raw prompt modal:** shows the system prompt as sent, and the message with its instructions block. Older history records show as they did before.

**Migration, and what I chose:**
- **Saved mode templates are left as they are.** Any `${SPEC_READING}` or `${PITON_FLUENCY}` in a mode or handoff template now fills in with nothing, and its paragraph drops out, so the fluency can't ride along on every prompt.
- **`system.md` is created with the default** the first time a project is prompted, like the other templates. If you'd removed the fluency from a mode template on purpose, edit `system.md` instead.
- **Queued prompts** get their instructions rebuilt from their mode when sent, because anchors queued before the upgrade still hold the old full system prompt, fluency included.
- **This repository's own templates changed too.** I removed the two placeholders from `ask.md`, `code.md`, `combined.md` and `spec.md` and added `system.md`. They're also the defaults baked into the app.

**Tests**
- **New test, `one_conversation_keeps_one_system_prompt`.** Using the fake harness, it sends Code, Spec, a Chain (spec step plus its handed-off code step), Ask and Freeform. It checks all six runs got the identical `--append-system-prompt`, equal to the project's. It checks each task's message carries its own instructions and its own understanding path, with the handoff in the chain's code step, and that none repeats the spec reading. It also checks that Freeform gets no instructions, and that a fresh Freeform conversation gets no system prompt.
- **Also new:**
  - tests for the instructions, the project system prompt and the migration, in `hidden_anchor.rs`;
  - one for the raw modal's message;
  - one for the Codex/OpenCode first-prompt-only rule.
- **Updated:**
  - the chain, handoff and raw-prompt tests, which read the message instead of the system prompt;
  - the defaults and settings tests.
- **Result:** the four tests that had been failing all session now pass. The full suite is 421 passing. `batch_sent_tasks_run_in_order_in_the_other_mode` and `raw_prompt_opens_once_the_task_has_compiled` fail now and then under a full run and pass when rerun alone, as before.

**Things to know**
- **Rebuild and restart the app** before any of this takes effect.
- **The first prompt of each new conversation still writes the whole system prompt to cache.** That can't be avoided, but it now happens once per conversation rather than on every prompt.
- **I ran `cargo fmt` on the whole crate,** which may have reformatted some of your other uncommitted Rust files.

**Spec changes to send in Spec mode:**
- `ModeSystemPromptsScope` (`spec/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.pi`):
  - A project-wide system template, `system.md`, holds the locations, SPEC_READING and PITON_FLUENCY. It's filled in as text, never compiled, and is identical for every prompt.
  - The mode and handoff templates are per-prompt instructions, with no SPEC_READING or PITON_FLUENCY; if a saved one still names them, they fill in as nothing.
  - The defaults section lists `system.md`, and the mode defaults no longer inject the spec reading or fluency.
- `PromptEditorShape.rawPrompt` (`spec/scope/prompt-mode/index.pi`):
  - "System prompt" is the project's.
  - "User prompt" is the message as sent, with its `<task-instructions>` block, and the record keeps the instructions.
  - Codex and OpenCode get the system prompt on a conversation's first prompt only.
- `HarnessIntegrationScope` (`spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi`):
  - Every prompt in a conversation, and every question, gets the same `--append-system-prompt`.
  - Freeform keeps the conversation's system prompt, and a new Freeform conversation gets none.
  - Codex and OpenCode get it ahead of the first prompt only.
- `ProjectDataScope.contents`: `system-prompts/` includes `system.md`, and a history record keeps the instructions and whether the run resumed a conversation.
- `SettingsWindowScope`: lists the System template first among the system prompts.
